notes: Rule of rules: a rule without evidence/grade is never loaded. grade=low can never be critical. If checked is older than 180 days the report flags it for re-verification.

rules.problem: robots.txt is missing or does not respond correctly
rules.action: Serve robots.txt as text/plain. If it returns HTML, crawlers cannot parse it

rules.problem: robots.txt is blocking the entire site
rules.action: Remove Disallow: /. If that is intentional, search visibility is impossible

rules.problem: no sitemap, or it is not declared in robots.txt
rules.action: Generate sitemap.xml and add one Sitemap: line to robots.txt. This is the discovery path Naver recommends

rules.problem: sitemap exceeds 50,000 URLs or 50MB uncompressed
rules.action: Split it using a sitemap index

rules.problem: sitemap contains relative URLs or URLs on another host (www/non-www, http/https mixed)
rules.action: Use absolute URLs on one canonical host

rules.problem: sitemap contains 404, redirecting or noindex URLs
rules.action: Remove them. A sitemap should list only indexable pages

rules.problem: sitemap entries have no lastmod, or the format is invalid
rules.action: Emit lastmod in W3C Datetime format. Crawlers use it to prioritise recrawls

rules.problem: home page is not a 200, or redirects twice or more
rules.action: Reduce the redirect chain to at most one hop

rules.problem: canonical is missing or does not point at the page itself
rules.action: Add a self-referencing canonical on the canonical host

rules.problem: title or meta description is missing, or duplicated across sampled pages
rules.action: Write a unique title and description per page

rules.problem: llms.txt is absent (which is not a problem)
rules.action: Optional. Google states it is unnecessary for AI features and measured traffic is near zero. Use --with-llms-txt if you want it for agent-readable docs

rules.problem: the initial HTML has almost no body text (JavaScript-rendered)
rules.action: Serve the body in the initial HTML via SSR or SSG. Crawlers and AI citation both read text

rules.problem: some internal links from the home page return 4xx or 5xx
rules.action: Fix the broken links

rules.problem: <html lang> does not match the actual content language
rules.action: Correct the lang attribute. It affects SEO, accessibility and market detection alike

rules.problem: Open Graph tags are missing
rules.action: Add og:title, og:description and og:image. These drive link previews in Slack, KakaoTalk, X and Facebook, not just Naver

rules.problem: IndexNow key file is missing
rules.action: Place the key file at the site root. It lets you notify Bing, Naver, Yandex and Seznam instantly (Google does not participate)

args.reason: ownership may already be verified by the HTML file method

rules.problem: google-site-verification meta tag is absent
rules.action: Pass the token from Search Console as --google-token and we will emit the tag. Ignore this if you already verified by file or DNS

rules.problem: noindex is applied (meta or X-Robots-Tag)
rules.action: Remove it unless intentional. A noindex page is excluded from both search and AI answers

rules.problem: nosnippet or max-snippet is suppressing snippets
rules.action: Remove it. Google's documentation makes AI Overviews and AI Mode citation conditional on being eligible to show with a snippet, so this blocks AI citation outright

rules.problem: Google-Extended policy status
rules.action: Blocking it has no effect on Google Search indexing (it only covers Gemini and Vertex training). Just confirm it matches your intent

rules.problem: JSON-LD structured data has a parse error
rules.action: Fix the syntax. This is for rich results; Google states it is not required for AI Overviews

rules.problem: the Indexing API may be in use for ordinary pages
rules.action: The Indexing API officially covers JobPosting and BroadcastEvent only. Ordinary pages belong in your sitemap with internal links

todo.label: Add the property in Search Console and submit the sitemap

rules.problem: Search Console registration and sitemap submission cannot be checked from outside
rules.action: Check it in the console yourself

args.reason: ownership may already be verified by the HTML file method, and that filename cannot be guessed

rules.problem: naver-site-verification meta tag is absent
rules.action: Pass the token from Search Advisor as --naver-token and we will place it in <head>. Ignore this if you already verified with the HTML file method

rules.problem: Naver's crawler Yeti is blocked in robots.txt
rules.action: Unblock Yeti. While blocked the site cannot appear in Naver search or AI Briefing at all

rules.problem: no RSS feed
rules.action: Generate one. RSS is nearly meaningless to Google and Bing, but Naver still treats it as a first-class input

todo.label: Register the site and verify ownership
todo.note: if the meta tag is already in place, you only need to press Verify in the console

todo.label: Submit the sitemap
todo.note: indexing takes about two weeks; not appearing during that window is normal

rules.problem: Search Advisor registration, RSS and sitemap submission cannot be verified
rules.action: There is no public API. Do it in the console in order: ownership, then RSS, then sitemap

args.reason: ownership may already be verified via DNS

rules.problem: no Bing ownership signal (msvalidate.01 or BingSiteAuth.xml)
rules.action: Pass --bing-token to emit the tag, or import the site from Google Search Console in one step

rules.problem: bingbot is blocked in robots.txt
rules.action: Unblock it. Bing's index also backs other AI search products, so the impact does not stop at Bing

todo.label: Register with Bing Webmaster Tools
todo.note: importing the site from Google Search Console takes about a minute

rules.problem: Bing Webmaster registration cannot be checked from outside
rules.action: Importing from Search Console is the fastest route

rules.problem: AI citation crawlers are blocked in robots.txt
rules.action: Training bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot) and citation bots (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) are separate tokens. Blocking the citation bots removes you from AI answers entirely

rules.problem: training crawler policy differs from the selected preset
rules.action: State your intent with --ai-policy=open|cite-only|closed. The default open maximises visibility; blocking training should be an explicit choice

rules.problem: user-triggered crawlers are blocked
rules.action: These are live fetches made when a person opens your link inside an AI product. Blocking them means users cannot open your page there

rules.problem: body content is buried in images (too little text per image)
rules.action: Provide the substance as text. Google's AI features guidance recommends keeping content in textual form

rules.problem: some sitemap pages are unreachable from the home page by internal links
rules.action: Add internal links. Google's AI features guidance explicitly recommends making content findable through internal links

rules.problem: few statistics, quotations or outbound citations
rules.action: Princeton's GEO study reported citation likelihood lifts of about +41% for quotations, +32% for statistics and +30% for inline citations. Those were interventions, not mere correlation, but results vary by domain and query

rules.problem: no structured elements such as lists or tables
rules.action: Informational only. Many AI-cited pages use lists, but that is correlation, not causation

rules.problem: Yahoo! JAPAN's own crawlers are blocked in robots.txt
rules.action: Unblock the Y!J-* family. Yahoo! JAPAN web search runs on Google's index, so GOOGLE rules cover ranking, but these crawlers feed Yahoo! JAPAN's own surfaces

args.note: Yahoo! JAPAN web search is powered by Google's index (about a third of Japan's search market), so your GOOGLE findings above apply to it. There is no separate submission console — use Google Search Console. Yahoo outside Japan is powered by Bing, so BING findings apply there.

rules.problem: how Yahoo is covered
rules.action: Nothing to do here. Fix the GOOGLE items to improve Yahoo! JAPAN, and the BING items to improve Yahoo elsewhere
